gates.name: 3 Printability
gates.detail: watertight, single component, fits bed; overhang brief 5.4 %, support risk 1.4 %

tells: Paired radii: inner_radius equals corner_radius (both 4) and outer_radius equals gusset_edge_radius (both 1). Each has a stated role, so this is a near-miss rather than a default-everything fillet, but the coincidence is worth one sentence in the docstring.

gusset_thickness 5 and gusset_reach 0.7 are chosen round numbers with no reason given in the brief or source (perimeter count, screw clearance, or stiffness target). Not a default, but not justified either.

fixes.text: State why gusset_thickness is 5 and gusset_reach is 0.7. A 5 mm rib is about 12 perimeters at 0.4 mm and the ramp foot at x=58 clears the shelf screws at x=44 by 14 mm; write that down or change the values to ones you can defend. No geometry change needed.

The wall holes sit at z=44, the centre of the free leg, because the brief's assumption says 'centred'. For pull-out the moment arm from the bottom edge would be longer with the pair nearer the top. Brief wins today; flag it for the next brief revision rather than changing the design.

The shelf counterbore floors are two 8 mm bridged rings at z=4.2 (the 68.7 mm2 of flat underside in the report). This is acknowledged and acceptable, but confirm on the first print that the ring did not sag into the counterbore, since a sagged floor lifts the screw head.

If a load test shows the wall leg delaminating across layers, print on a side face (y=-30 down) instead. That aligns both legs and the rib with the load and keeps all four counterbores as teardrops. Only do this if the test fails; the brief pins shelf-face-down.
